Somos un par de estudiantes de tecnicatura en electrónica y electromecánica; contamos con conocimientos físicos-mecanicos y hardware electrónico.

Buscamos gente comprometida. Preferentemente en cercanías, para poder presentar un proyecto destacado.

A su vez, buscamos en lo posible, gente que tenga conocimientos en programación y armado de webs/apps/software's.
summary:
Wildfire seasons are treated as uniform across a country, but they are not. GUARDIA builds an
operational fire-risk calendar for 68 departments across three Argentine provinces — Corrientes,
Córdoba and Entre Ríos — using 26 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire records. For each department it
answers three questions: which weeks concentrate 80% of its historical activity, which week holds
the historical maximum, and which weeks exceeded the 90th percentile of previous years. A
concentration index (Gini) classifies each territory from compact to dispersed, and the season
expected from the scientific literature is drawn as a reference band behind the observed data.
The result exposes what a single national average hides: in the Iberá wetlands the peak falls in
February, outside the expected season, because a drought-driven regime dominates the record,
while in the Sierras the season is compact. Civil-defence teams can then concentrate brigades,
burn bans and patrols in the weeks that actually matter.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

GUARDIA converts 26 years of satellite fire detections into an operational calendar per department. For each of the 68 departments it returns the critical core — the weeks that accumulate 80% of the historical activity — the historical maximum week with its year, the weeks that exceeded the 90th percentile of previous years, and a concentration index that classifies the territory from compact to dispersed. It also draws the season expected from the scientific literature as a reference band, so any divergence between expectation and observation becomes visible instead of being averaged away. The application also compares any two departments over the same 53 weeks — to see whether neighbouring territories share a season — and exports each department's weekly series as CSV, so the calendar can be taken into a spreadsheet or a report.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Active-fire detections from NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, 1 km; VIIRS C2 375 m, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21) are cropped to the bounding boxes of the three provinces for 2000-11-01 to 2026-11-13.

2. Each detection is assigned to a department polygon by point-in-polygon. Detections falling outside the 68 departmental polygons (33.63% of 1,045,996) are discarded and the figure is stated in the Method page.

3. Detections are aggregated by ISO week and the weeks are ranked by accumulated volume until 80% of the department total is reached. That set is the critical core.

4. The typical week is the one with the largest accumulated volume; the historical maximum is the single worst week of the series, reported with its year, because one extreme season can dominate a 26-year record.

5. Anomalies use the 90th percentile computed only from years prior to the year being evaluated, never including the year itself, and no anomaly is flagged with fewer than five prior years.

6. The Gini coefficient of the 53 weekly totals measures concentration: 0.75 and above means a compact window, below 0.45 means activity spread through the year.

BENEFITS

A civil-defence office cannot sustain maximum alert for twelve months. GUARDIA tells it which weeks of the year carry the risk, with the number that justifies the decision, and shows when the observed record departs from the expected season. It also makes satellite-era changes explicit: before April 2018 the record is MODIS only, and from April 2018 it includes VIIRS, so steps in the series are instrument changes, not necessarily more fire.

INTENDED IMPACT

A reproducible method any municipality can run for its own department, at a scale where decisions are actually taken, rather than a national average that hides the local season.

CREATIVITY

The insight is that the fire season is not a property of a province but of a department, and that some territories have two regimes that never appear in the same month. Making the literature's expected season visible next to the observed data turns a dashboard into an argument: the reader sees a February peak sitting outside the August-September band and understands that the extreme regime dominates the record.

TOOLS AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

Python for ingestion and computation (no external geospatial libraries: the point-in-polygon test is implemented in the project). Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind for the interface, with an SVG choropleth generated from the departmental polygons, so the page needs no tile server and loads on a low-end phone. Factors weighed: comparability over precision, honest treatment of missing and discarded data, performance on mobile, and the difference between what the literature expects and what the record shows.

LIMITS

The product does not predict fire, does not measure burned area, and is not validated against ground truth. Detections are near-real-time active-fire anomalies, not fire perimeters. The 33.63% of detections outside departmental polygons are excluded and declared.
